Neighbor 1 is a positive analog overall, but it is mixed. The query has much higher estimated logP than the neighbor (1.715 vs 0.3564, delta +1.3586), and that shift is unfavorable because BBB penetration is usually helped by moderate lipophilicity rather than an overly polar profile, so the comparison here is counted against crossing. At the same time, the query also has a higher neutral fraction (0.566 vs 0.3942, delta +0.1718), which is favorable for membrane passage, and the query is less flexible in the relevant sense because fraction of sp3 carbons drops from 0.2 to 0 (delta -0.2), which in this context aligns with the more BBB-like side of the comparison. The shared thiazole and identical topological polar surface area of 77.29 Å² mean those features do not separate the pair, while the increase in rotatable-bond count from 1 to 2 (delta +1) is a small flexibility penalty. Taken together, Neighbor 1 still leans toward the BBB-crossing label because the neutral fraction and reduced sp3 content support it, even though higher logP, shared thiazole, unchanged TPSA, and one extra rotatable bond pull the other way.

Neighbor 2 is another positive analog, and its evidence also cuts in both directions. The absence of sulfonic derivative, sulfuric derivative, and sulfonamide in the query is a strong favorable difference here, since the neighbor contains those highly polar functionalities while the query does not. The query’s estimated logP is much higher (1.715 vs -0.768, delta +2.483), but in this local comparison that higher lipophilicity is treated as unfavorable relative to the BBB-crossing neighbor. The query also has a much lower topological polar surface area (77.29 vs 175.83, delta -98.54), which is strongly favorable because the query sits back in the CNS-friendly TPSA region while the neighbor is far above it. In addition, the query has fewer basic sites (2 vs 5, delta -3), which reduces ionizable burden and again supports BBB penetration. The only significant feature that cuts against the query is the much lower polarity of the neighbor’s sulfonated scaffold; because the query avoids those groups and has reduced basic-site burden plus much lower TPSA, Neighbor 2 overall supports the BBB-crossing label.

Neighbor 3 is also a positive analog and provides some of the clearest support. The neighbor’s TPSA is 137.5 Å², far above the favorable BBB range, while the query sits at 77.29 Å²; that 60.21 Å² drop is a major improvement for crossing. The query also has lower nitrogen/oxygen atom count, 4 instead of 8 (delta -4), which fits the lower heteroatom burden expected for BBB permeation. The query lacks the neighbor’s nitrile and dialkyl thioether, and it has only one guanidine versus the neighbor’s two copies, all of which is helpful because the neighbor is carrying more polar/basic functionality. The one opposing factor is that the query has higher estimated logP (1.715 vs -0.0727, delta +1.7877), which in this pair is treated as unfavorable relative to the neighbor, but that lipophilicity shift does not outweigh the large gains from lower TPSA, fewer N/O atoms, and fewer guanidine-like basic groups. Overall, Neighbor 3 strongly reinforces the BBB-crossing label.

Neighbor 4 is a negative analog, but it actually contains a few features that make the query look more BBB-like. The query has guanidine once while the neighbor has none, and that difference is unfavorable for the query because guanidine adds a strongly polar/basic element. The query also has slightly higher QED drug-likeness (0.5948 vs 0.5852, delta +0.0096), which is not enough to offset the polarity penalties. The neighbor’s strongest acidic pKa is 11.8771 while the query has no acidic site; that specific comparison is handled as favorable for the query on this pair, but it is not the dominant feature. The query has fewer basic sites (2 vs 7, delta -5), which is favorable for BBB penetration, and it does contain thiazole once while the neighbor does not, but that feature is still counted against the query in this local comparison. The query’s maximum partial charge is slightly lower (0.2124 vs 0.2237, delta -0.0113), which is also modestly favorable. Even though this negative neighbor does not perfectly align with the label, the query is still somewhat more BBB-compatible on several of the key descriptors, so this comparison does not overturn the overall BBB-crossing case.

Neighbor 5 is the other negative analog and is more clearly informative. The neighbor has oxazole, while the query does not, and the query also has guanidine once while the neighbor has none; both of those features are unfavorable because they add heteroatom/polar burden relative to the query side being compared. The query has lower fraction of sp3 carbons (0 vs 0.1111, delta -0.1111), which in this local context is also unfavorable, and it has a higher TPSA (77.29 vs 63.33, delta +13.96), moving away from the more compact polar profile seen in the neighbor. The NH/OH group count is much higher in the query (4 vs 1, delta +3), which is a clear disadvantage because donor burden is a major BBB penalty. The one feature that runs the other way is maximum partial charge, where the query is lower (0.2124 vs 0.3034, delta -0.091), a small favorable shift. But the combined effect of oxazole absence, guanidine presence, lower sp3 fraction, higher TPSA, and more NH/OH groups makes this negative neighbor support the non-crossing side more than the crossing side, even if one charge metric slightly favors the query.

Neighbor 6 is the last negative analog and again gives a mixed but still useful picture. The query has slightly higher TPSA than the neighbor (77.29 vs 76.76, delta +0.53), which is a small disadvantage because the neighbor is already in the borderline low-70s region while the query moves upward. The query has guanidine while the neighbor does not, which is unfavorable, and the query also contains thiazole once while the neighbor does not, another feature that in this comparison is not helping. The query’s estimated logD is higher (1.4678 vs 0.6132, delta +0.8546), which is generally more consistent with BBB permeation than a very low logD, but here it still appears in a negative-neighbor comparison where the surrounding structural context is less favorable. The strongest favorable differences are that the neighbor has a strongest acidic pKa of 7.9572 while the query has no acidic site, and the query has a slightly higher maximum partial charge difference only by a very small margin (0.2124 vs 0.2107, delta +0.0017), which is not enough to carry the comparison. Because this negative analog is already close in TPSA and logD, the remaining guanidine and thiazole burden still make it a reasonable non-crossing reference, though the query retains enough favorable characteristics that the direction is not purely one-sided.

Putting the six neighbors together, the three positive neighbors consistently highlight the query’s lower TPSA than the strongly polar analogs, its lower N/O burden, fewer basic sites than heavily ionized scaffolds, and its better neutral-fraction or reduced sp3 profile, all of which are compatible with BBB penetration. The three negative neighbors are more mixed, but even there the query often shows the kinds of features associated with BBB permeability: lower basic-site burden, no sulfonated groups, and in some cases lower charge or better logD. The most important recurring pattern is that the query avoids the very high TPSA and strong polar-functional-group burdens seen in the non-crossing neighbors, while staying in the more favorable TPSA region around 77 Å² that is commonly compatible with brain entry. Taken together, the neighborhood evidence supports option (B): crosses the BBB.
